title: Zooming in on the circumgalactic medium with GIBLE: Cloud-scale simulations with cosmological initial conditions
comment: Submitted to PASA; 13 pages, 7 figures (main draft)
summary: We conduct simulations of $\sim$kpc-scale cool clouds in the circumgalactic medium (CGM), using initial conditions sampled from a highly resolved cosmological magneto-hydrodynamical zoom-in of a Milky Way-like galaxy. We select ten distinct cold clouds with masses of $m_{\rm{cloud}}$ $\sim$ $10^{4.5-5}$ M$_\odot$, originally resolved at a mass resolution of $m_{\rm{gas}}$ $\sim$ $200$ M$_\odot$. To further resolve small-scale features and physics, we implement a targeted refinement scheme within spherical regions co-moving with each cloud, thereby boosting the local mass resolution by a factor of 1000, reaching $m_{\rm{gas}}$ $\sim$ $0.2$ M$_\odot$ (spatial resolution, $r_{\rm{gas,cloud}}$ $\sim$ $O(\rm{pc})$). The selected clouds have diverse properties, across a broad parameter space, resulting in heterogeneous evolution. For the clouds we study, radiative cooling is the dominant physical process enabling cloud survival, while magnetic fields play a comparatively smaller role. The motion of these clouds is governed not only by drag forces that decelerate them, but also by acceleration from momentum exchange with the complex background velocity field, which can cause them to move faster than ballistic projectiles set by their initial velocities. Our results suggest that the non-trivial details of realistic cosmological initial conditions -- specifically the complex density, temperature, and velocity fields -- may play an important role in subsequent cloud evolution, and that sampling the output of an existing large-scale simulation provides a self-consistent approach to capture these effects without ad hoc assumptions.

AI.tldr: High-resolution simulations of kpc-scale cool clouds in the CGM using cosmological initial conditions show that radiative cooling enables cloud survival, while magnetic fields play a minor role, and complex background velocity fields can accelerate clouds beyond ballistic predictions.
AI.motivation: To understand the evolution of cool clouds in the circumgalactic medium with realistic cosmological initial conditions, avoiding ad hoc assumptions about cloud properties and environment.
AI.method: Used initial conditions from a high-resolution cosmological MHD zoom-in simulation of a Milky Way-like galaxy, selected ten distinct cold clouds, and implemented targeted refinement to boost local mass resolution by 1000x (to ~0.2 M⊙, ~pc spatial resolution).
AI.result: Radiative cooling is dominant for cloud survival; magnetic fields play a smaller role. Clouds experience both drag deceleration and acceleration from momentum exchange with complex background velocity fields, sometimes moving faster than ballistic predictions.
AI.conclusion: Realistic cosmological initial conditions (complex density, temperature, and velocity fields) significantly impact cloud evolution, and sampling from existing large-scale simulations provides a self-consistent approach to capture these effects.

title: Starbursts hiding in the main sequence: a pathway toward quenching?
comment: submitted to the Open Journal of Astrophysics
summary: Star-forming galaxies spend most of their lifetimes on the star-forming main sequence, which establishes a tight empirical and statistical relation between stellar mass and star-formation rate. Occasional episodes of rapid star formation can push them temporarily above this sequence, turning them into starbursts. Yet some galaxies display starburst-like traits -- rapid, dense, and compact star formation -- while still remaining within the scatter of the main sequence. These "starbursts in the main sequence" (SBMSs) reveal the complexity and diversity of star formation modes, making them crucial for understanding how galaxies evolve and transition between different regimes. In this paper, we identify SBMSs in the cosmological simulation NewHorizon and follow their evolution across time to uncover their physical origins and the role of this special regime in shaping galaxy evolution. We explain the existence of SBMSs by a comparatively earlier assembly of their stellar mass, driven in particular by more frequent and repeated mergers as the other galaxies, as well as exceptionally productive starburst events triggered by these interactions. As a result, this regime appears preferentially -- though not exclusively -- in the most massive galaxies. The SBMS behavior is not continuous within individual galaxies but instead arises intermittently as a short-lived (~ 30 Myr) evolutionary mode. Nevertheless, such SBMS episodes exist throughout cosmic time across the galaxy population... [abridged]

AI.tldr: Galaxies can exhibit starburst-like characteristics while remaining within the main sequence scatter, forming a distinct "starbursts in the main sequence" (SBMS) regime driven by early stellar assembly and repeated mergers.
AI.motivation: To understand the physical origins and evolutionary significance of galaxies that display starburst-like traits (rapid, dense, compact star formation) while still statistically residing within the main sequence scatter, revealing complexity in star formation modes and galaxy evolution transitions.
AI.method: Identification and temporal tracking of SBMS galaxies in the cosmological simulation NewHorizon, analyzing their evolution to uncover physical drivers including stellar mass assembly timing, merger frequency, and starburst event productivity.
AI.result: SBMS existence explained by comparatively earlier stellar mass assembly driven by more frequent/repeated mergers and exceptionally productive starburst events triggered by interactions, preferentially appearing in massive galaxies as intermittent, short-lived (~30 Myr) evolutionary episodes occurring throughout cosmic time.
AI.conclusion: SBMS represents a distinct, intermittent evolutionary mode where galaxies temporarily exhibit starburst characteristics while remaining statistically within the main sequence, driven by merger-enhanced early stellar assembly, revealing important complexity in galaxy evolution pathways.

title: Constraining the mass of the M31 ionized baryon Halo using CHIME/FRB Catalog 2
comment: 23 pages, 8 figures, 2 tables. Submitted to ApJ
summary: The circumgalactic medium (CGM) surrounding galaxies is believed to be a significant reservoir of baryons, yet its total mass remains poorly constrained. We present a novel approach to probe the CGM of the Andromeda galaxy (M31) using fast radio bursts (FRBs) from the CHIME/FRB Catalog 2. By comparing the dispersion measures (DMs) of 171 FRBs whose sightlines intersect M31's halo (within $r_{\rm vir}= 302\,\mathrm{kpc}$) to a control sample of 684 FRBs, we estimate the DM contribution from M31's CGM. We find evidence for an excess DM of $δ\mathrm{DM} = 5.9$--$59.6\,\mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}}$ in the inner halo ($\approx 0$--$151\,\mathrm{kpc}$) and $δ\mathrm{DM} = 25.7$--$64.6\,\mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}}$ in the outer halo ($\approx 151$--$302\,\mathrm{kpc}$). Using a generalized halo model parameterized by a closure radius $r_{\mathrm{close}}$, we constrain the baryon distribution and infer a best-fit value for $r_{\mathrm{close}}$ to be $9.2^{+9.9}_{-4.9}\,r_{\rm vir}$ ($1σ$), corresponding to a total CGM mass of $M_{b,\mathrm{halo}} = 18.6^{+7.9}_{-8.4} \times 10^{10}\,M_\odot$. Our results suggest that M31 may harbor a substantial fraction of its cosmic baryon budget in diffuse, ionized gas. This work demonstrates the potential of FRBs as a powerful tool for studying the CGM of nearby galaxies, with future larger samples expected to provide tighter constraints on the baryon content of galactic halos.

AI.tldr: Using FRBs from CHIME/FRB Catalog 2 to probe M31's circumgalactic medium, researchers detected excess dispersion measures in both inner and outer halo regions, inferring a substantial CGM mass of ~1.86×10¹¹ M☉, suggesting M31 may harbor a significant fraction of its cosmic baryon budget in diffuse ionized gas.
AI.motivation: The circumgalactic medium (CGM) is believed to be a significant reservoir of baryons, but its total mass remains poorly constrained. There is a need for novel approaches to probe the CGM of nearby galaxies like Andromeda (M31) to better understand baryon distribution in galactic halos.
AI.method: Used fast radio bursts (FRBs) from the CHIME/FRB Catalog 2 to probe M31's CGM. Compared dispersion measures (DMs) of 171 FRBs whose sightlines intersect M31's halo (within r_vir=302 kpc) to a control sample of 684 FRBs. Applied a generalized halo model parameterized by a closure radius r_close to constrain baryon distribution.
AI.result: Found evidence for excess DM of 5.9-59.6 pc cm⁻³ in inner halo (0-151 kpc) and 25.7-64.6 pc cm⁻³ in outer halo (151-302 kpc). Best-fit closure radius r_close = 9.2^{+9.9}_{-4.9} r_vir (1σ), corresponding to total CGM mass M_b,halo = 18.6^{+7.9}_{-8.4} × 10¹⁰ M☉.
AI.conclusion: M31 may harbor a substantial fraction of its cosmic baryon budget in diffuse, ionized gas. FRBs demonstrate potential as a powerful tool for studying CGM of nearby galaxies, with future larger samples expected to provide tighter constraints on baryon content of galactic halos.

title: nanoCMB: A minimal CMB power spectrum calculator in Python
summary: We present nanoCMB, a minimal but accurate calculator for the unlensed CMB temperature and polarisation angular power spectra ($C_\ell^{TT}$, $C_\ell^{EE}$, $C_\ell^{TE}$) of flat $Λ$CDM cosmologies. Written in $\sim$1400 lines of readable Python, the code implements the full line-of-sight integration method: RECFAST recombination, coupled Einstein--Boltzmann perturbation equations in synchronous gauge with a tight-coupling approximation, precomputed spherical Bessel function tables, and optimally constructed non-uniform grids in wavenumber and conformal time. Despite its brevity, nanoCMB achieves sub-percent agreement with CAMB across the multipole range $2 \le \ell \le 2500$, running in $\sim$10 seconds on a modern laptop. The entire calculation lives in a single, easily modifiable Python script, designed as a pedagogical bridge between textbook treatments and research-level Boltzmann solvers, with every approximation and numerical choice made explicit. We describe the physics, equations, and computational methods in detail, with code snippets illustrating each stage of the calculation. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/adammoss/nanoCMB.

AI.tldr: nanoCMB is a minimal Python calculator for unlensed CMB power spectra that achieves sub-percent accuracy compared to CAMB while being compact (~1400 lines) and running in ~10 seconds.
AI.motivation: To create a pedagogical bridge between textbook treatments and research-level Boltzmann solvers, providing a minimal but accurate CMB calculator with explicit approximations and numerical choices for educational purposes.
AI.method: Implements full line-of-sight integration method with RECFAST recombination, coupled Einstein-Boltzmann perturbation equations in synchronous gauge with tight-coupling approximation, precomputed spherical Bessel function tables, and optimally constructed non-uniform grids in wavenumber and conformal time.
AI.result: Achieves sub-percent agreement with CAMB across multipole range 2 ≤ ℓ ≤ 2500, runs in ~10 seconds on a modern laptop, and provides a single, easily modifiable Python script for educational use.
AI.conclusion: nanoCMB successfully bridges the gap between theoretical understanding and complex research tools, offering an accessible, transparent, and accurate CMB calculator for pedagogical purposes while maintaining computational efficiency.

title: Predicting Resolved Dust Attenuation from Local Galaxy Properties Using MaNGA
summary: Accurate spatially resolved dust corrections are critical for interpreting the structure and evolution of star-forming galaxies (SFGs). We present an empirical model for predicting spatially resolved dust attenuation ($A_V$) in SFGs using integral field spectroscopy from the Mapping Nearby Galaxies at Apache Point Observatory (MaNGA) survey. Using a sample of 5,155 galaxies over $7.20<M_\ast<11.14$ and $0.0002 < z < 0.1444$, we derive $A_V$ maps from the Balmer decrement across more than 1,898,954 star-forming spaxels. Using local star formation rate surface density ($Σ_{\text{SFR}}$) as a predictor, the model achieves $R^2 = 0.69$ and RMSE $=0.22$ mag, with residuals that are approximately Gaussian and centred near zero. It predicts $A_V$ within a factor of $\sim$1.3 on kpc scales. We also demonstrate that the relation can be applied iteratively to recover dust-corrected $Σ_{\mathrm{SFR}}$ from uncorrected values, converging by the fourth iteration with minimal residual bias ($-0.01$ mag) and low RMSE ($0.42$ mag). The model accurately reproduces $A_V$ maps across diverse morphologies and orientations, including edge-on systems. It also recovers the observed radial $A_V$ profiles, capturing their dependence on stellar mass and relative star formation activity, with more massive and more strongly star-forming galaxies showing steeper gradients.

AI.tldr: Empirical model predicts spatially resolved dust attenuation (A_V) in star-forming galaxies using local star formation rate surface density, achieving high accuracy on kpc scales and enabling iterative recovery of dust-corrected star formation rates.
AI.motivation: Accurate spatially resolved dust corrections are critical for interpreting the structure and evolution of star-forming galaxies, as dust attenuation affects measurements of star formation rates and galaxy properties.
AI.method: Develop empirical model using MaNGA integral field spectroscopy data from 5,155 galaxies. Derive A_V maps from Balmer decrement across 1.9 million star-forming spaxels. Use local star formation rate surface density (Σ_SFR) as predictor for dust attenuation.
AI.result: Model achieves R² = 0.69 and RMSE = 0.22 mag, predicting A_V within factor ~1.3 on kpc scales. Can be applied iteratively to recover dust-corrected Σ_SFR from uncorrected values, converging by fourth iteration with minimal residual bias (-0.01 mag) and low RMSE (0.42 mag). Accurately reproduces A_V maps across diverse morphologies and captures radial A_V profiles dependent on stellar mass and star formation activity.
AI.conclusion: The empirical model provides accurate spatially resolved dust attenuation predictions using local star formation rate surface density, enabling better interpretation of galaxy structure and evolution. It captures systematic trends where more massive and more strongly star-forming galaxies show steeper dust attenuation gradients.

title: Dark Acoustic Oscillations and the Hubble Tension
summary: The Hubble tension and the recently reported anomaly in data from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) are considered to pose serious challenges to the standard $Λ$CDM model of cosmology. In this work, we show that resolving the Hubble tension with a scenario featuring dark radiation-matter decoupling (DRMD) predicts the presence of dark acoustic oscillations (DAO) similar in scale to baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO). Using an inference independent of large-scale structure data, relying only on Planck measurements of the cosmic microwave background and SH$0$ES-calibrated supernova data, we find evidence for a DAO signal with drag-horizon scale $r_{d,\mathrm{DAO}} \in[54,65]\,\mathrm{Mpc}/h$ ($68\%\,\mathrm{C.I.}$) and amplitude $A_\mathrm{DAO} \in [0.02,0.05]$ ($68\%\,\mathrm{C.I.}$). These predictions provide a concrete target for current and upcoming large-scale structure surveys, including DESI, Euclid, and the Roman Space Telescope. Remarkably, the predicted DAO properties are consistent with those required to explain the DESI anomaly, offering both an alternative to evolving dark energy and a preliminary validation of the relevance of a dark radiation-matter decoupling scenario for addressing the Hubble tension.

AI.tldr: DRMD scenario resolving Hubble tension predicts DAO signal consistent with DESI anomaly, providing alternative to evolving dark energy.
AI.motivation: Address Hubble tension and DESI anomaly challenges to ΛCDM cosmology by exploring dark radiation-matter decoupling scenario.
AI.method: Use Planck CMB measurements and SH0ES-calibrated supernova data for inference independent of large-scale structure data to detect DAO signal.
AI.result: Found evidence for DAO signal with drag-horizon scale rd,DAO ∈ [54,65] Mpc/h and amplitude ADAO ∈ [0.02,0.05] (68% C.I.), consistent with DESI anomaly requirements.
AI.conclusion: DRMD scenario offers both resolution to Hubble tension and explanation for DESI anomaly, providing testable predictions for current/future surveys.

title: The capture of halo material by orbiting subhaloes
summary: When a dark matter halo falls into a more massive object and becomes a subhalo, it typically loses much of its mass through tidal stripping. The reverse process is also possible in principle. The subhalo may gravitationally capture material from its host. If sufficiently efficient, this process could make an initially starless subhalo visible. We use high-resolution N-body simulations to estimate the efficiency of capture. We find that after an extended period orbiting within its host, at most $\sim 10^{-4}$ of a subhalo's remaining mass has been acquired since infall. This captured material is less concentrated to subhalo centre than material retained from before infall. It is also very much less abundant than host material that is instantaneously passing through the subhalo on almost unperturbed orbits. Captured stars are not sufficiently spatially concentrated to be distinguished from the dominant background of "field" stars, and their concentration in velocity space is no greater than that of typical stellar streams in the halo. Unfortunately, stellar capture is not efficient enough to allow initially starless low-mass subhaloes to be detected.

AI.tldr: Dark matter subhalos can theoretically capture stars from their host galaxies, but simulations show this process is extremely inefficient (~10⁻⁴ mass fraction), making starless subhalos undetectable through stellar capture.
AI.motivation: To investigate whether dark matter subhalos can become visible by gravitationally capturing stars from their host galaxies, potentially allowing detection of initially starless low-mass subhalos.
AI.method: High-resolution N-body simulations to estimate the efficiency of gravitational capture of material from host galaxies by subhalos.
AI.result: After extended orbital periods, at most ~10⁻⁴ of a subhalo's remaining mass is captured material; captured stars are less concentrated than retained material and indistinguishable from background field stars.
AI.conclusion: Stellar capture is too inefficient to make initially starless low-mass subhalos detectable, as captured stars cannot be distinguished from the dominant background of field stars or stellar streams.

title: Probing inflationary features with galaxy ultraviolet luminosity function observables
summary: We use the galaxy ultraviolet luminosity function measurements at $z=6-9$ to constrain modification to standard inflationary power spectrum. These observables are sensitive to the matter power spectrum which itself depends on inflationary initial conditions. We consider specific models where a bump or oscillatory features are introduced to the standard power law inflation spectrum. We find that the galaxy luminosity observables can probe such modifications at wavenumbers $0.5\lesssim k \lesssim 20$ Mpc$^{-1}$. We obtain upper limits on the amplitude of bump-like features at the mentioned wavenumbers. We obtain constraints which are similar to previous constraints on these models using measurements of optical depth of reionization. However, the galaxy luminosity functions are a more direct probe for these type of models and, therefore, can complement indirect constraints coming from measurements of IGM properties.

AI.tldr: Galaxy UV luminosity functions at z=6-9 constrain inflationary power spectrum modifications (bumps/oscillatory features) at k ~ 0.5-20 Mpc⁻¹, providing direct probes complementary to reionization optical depth constraints.
AI.motivation: To use high-redshift galaxy observations as direct probes of inflationary physics by constraining modifications to the primordial power spectrum, complementing indirect constraints from IGM properties.
AI.method: Analyze galaxy ultraviolet luminosity function measurements at redshifts 6-9 to constrain modifications to the standard inflationary power spectrum, specifically considering models with bump-like or oscillatory features added to the standard power-law spectrum.
AI.result: Galaxy luminosity observables can probe inflationary modifications at wavenumbers 0.5 ≲ k ≲ 20 Mpc⁻¹, with obtained upper limits on bump feature amplitudes similar to previous constraints from reionization optical depth measurements.
AI.conclusion: High-redshift galaxy luminosity functions provide a more direct probe of inflationary modifications than indirect IGM property measurements, offering complementary constraints on primordial power spectrum features.

title: Timing and scintillation of a young Galactic halo pulsar
summary: We present a timing and scintillation study of the young Galactic halo pulsar PSR J1740+1000 using observations from the Nanshan, FAST, and Parkes radio telescopes. From timing analysis, we measure the pulsar's proper motion for the first time, indicating motion away from the Galactic plane at a position angle of 16.7 +/- 4.8 degrees (Galactic coordinates), with a total proper motion of 56.9 +/- 8.0 mas/yr and a corresponding transverse velocity of 329 +/- 80 km/s. This velocity suggests that PSR J1740+1000 is a typical-velocity young pulsar born within the Galactic halo. In scintillation studies, we detect scintillation arcs, arclets, and double-layered adjacent arcs in the secondary spectra. Under isotropic and anisotropic scattering assumptions, the screen-to-pulsar distance is 370 +/- 72 pc and 1 +/- 12 pc, respectively. The latter closely matches the scale of the pulsar wind nebula associated with PSR J1740+1000 and provides a better fit, suggesting that scattering is likely dominated by the PWN. The double-layered adjacent arcs observed on MJD 60180 imply that the pulsar's scattered image consists of two dominant components (A and B) and multiple weaker components. Component A is located at the pulsar's geometric position (0 uas), while Component B is located 112 +/- 16 uas and 23 +/- 17 uas from the central component under isotropic and anisotropic scattering, respectively. The frequency-independent angular position of Component B hints at refraction by an AU-scale structure within the scattering region, possibly originating from the PWN.

AI.tldr: First proper motion measurement of young Galactic halo pulsar PSR J1740+1000 reveals high transverse velocity (329 km/s) and motion away from Galactic plane. Scintillation studies show arcs suggesting scattering dominated by pulsar wind nebula, with double-layered arcs indicating multiple scattering components including one possibly refracted by AU-scale PWN structure.
AI.motivation: To characterize the kinematic properties and interstellar scattering environment of the young Galactic halo pulsar PSR J1740+1000 through precise timing and scintillation analysis, aiming to understand its origin, motion, and the nature of its scattering screen.
AI.method: Combined timing analysis using Nanshan, FAST, and Parkes radio telescope observations to measure proper motion, and scintillation studies analyzing secondary spectra to detect arcs, arclets, and double-layered adjacent arcs, applying both isotropic and anisotropic scattering models.
AI.result: First proper motion measurement: total proper motion 56.9±8.0 mas/yr, transverse velocity 329±80 km/s, moving away from Galactic plane at position angle 16.7±4.8°. Scintillation analysis reveals screen-to-pulsar distances of 370±72 pc (isotropic) and 1±12 pc (anisotropic), with anisotropic model better matching PWN scale. Double-layered arcs show two dominant scattering components, with Component B offset 112±16 uas (isotropic) or 23±17 uas (anisotropic) from central component.
AI.conclusion: PSR J1740+1000 is a typical-velocity young pulsar born in the Galactic halo. Scattering is likely dominated by its pulsar wind nebula rather than general interstellar medium, with double-layered arcs suggesting multiple scattering components and possible refraction by AU-scale structures within the PWN.

title: A Unified Origin of Primordial Black Hole Dark Matter and Nanohertz Gravitational Waves
summary: Recent high-cadence observations by Subaru-HSC have identified a population of ultrashort-timescale microlensing events, providing a compelling window for planet-mass primordial black holes (PBHs) to constitute the entirety of dark matter. In this Letter, we demonstrate that this PBH population and the nanohertz stochastic gravitational-wave (GW) background reported by pulsar timing arrays (PTAs) can be naturally unified by a single primordial origin: a broad, nearly-flat enhancement of the curvature power spectrum with an amplitude of $O(10^{-2})$. The resulting PBH mass function spans the planet-to-solar mass range, while remaining consistent with all current observational constraints. This unified PBH--induced-GW framework makes concrete multi-messenger predictions, which can be decisively scrutinized by forthcoming microlensing surveys, next-generation PTAs, space-borne interferometers, precision astrometry, and laser ranging experiments.

AI.tldr: Unified framework connects ultrashort microlensing events (planet-mass PBHs as dark matter) with nanohertz GW background via single primordial curvature power spectrum enhancement.
AI.motivation: To provide a unified explanation for two recent astrophysical observations: Subaru-HSC ultrashort-timescale microlensing events suggesting planet-mass PBHs as dark matter, and PTA-detected nanohertz stochastic GW background.
AI.method: Proposes a single primordial origin: a broad, nearly-flat enhancement of the curvature power spectrum with amplitude ~10^-2, generating PBHs with mass function spanning planet-to-solar masses while remaining consistent with observational constraints.
AI.result: The model naturally unifies both phenomena - PBH population explains microlensing events, while induced GWs from same primordial perturbations explain PTA GW background.
AI.conclusion: This unified PBH-induced-GW framework makes testable multi-messenger predictions that can be scrutinized by future microlensing surveys, next-gen PTAs, space interferometers, astrometry, and laser ranging experiments.

title: Age and metallicity of the Milky Way's nuclear star cluster studied at 3 pc from Sagittarius A*
summary:
The Milky Way's nuclear star cluster (NSC) is a unique laboratory to study the formation and evolution of dense stellar systems around a supermassive black hole. Previous work suggests that most stars in the NSC are old; however, the detailed age and metallicity distributions remain uncertain. We constrain the star formation history (SFH) and metallicity of a poorly explored region located $\sim$3 pc from SagittariusA*.
  We analyse VLT/NACO imaging in an intermediate-band filter centred at 2.24 $μ$m, complemented by $H$-band data. We construct completeness-corrected $K$-band luminosity functions (LFs), clearly identifying the Red Clump and Red Giant Branch Bumps. The SFH is derived by fitting cumulative LFs with MIST, PARSEC, and BaSTI models spanning a wide range of ages and metallicities, using Monte Carlo sampling to estimate uncertainties. Metallicity constraints are refined using spectroscopic measurements from the literature.
  The stellar population is predominantly old and metal-rich: $75.6 \pm 9.5$% of the stellar mass formed $\gtrsim 10$ Gyr ago, with median [M/H] $\sim +0.35$. An intermediate-age component at 2-3 Gyr contributes $20.8 \pm 8.7$%, while minor populations are present at $\sim$400 Myr ($0.9 \pm 0.8$%) and 20 Myr ($3.6 \pm 1.4$%), the latter representing a small but non-negligible young population. Systematic uncertainties from stellar models, binning, photometric range, unresolved binaries, and filter choice are assessed.
  These results indicate early dominant formation, a significant 2-3 Gyr episode, and minor recent activity, consistent with spectroscopic measurements and with properties of the inner NSC and nuclear stellar disc.

AI.tldr: The Milky Way's nuclear star cluster near Sgr A* is predominantly old and metal-rich, with 75.6% of stellar mass formed >10 Gyr ago, plus significant 2-3 Gyr and minor recent star formation episodes.
AI.motivation: The Milky Way's nuclear star cluster is a unique laboratory for studying dense stellar systems around supermassive black holes, but detailed age and metallicity distributions remain uncertain, particularly in regions ~3 pc from Sgr A*.
AI.method: Used VLT/NACO imaging in 2.24 μm intermediate-band filter with H-band data, constructed completeness-corrected K-band luminosity functions to identify Red Clump and Red Giant Branch Bumps. Derived star formation history by fitting cumulative LFs with MIST, PARSEC, and BaSTI models using Monte Carlo sampling, refined metallicity constraints with literature spectroscopic measurements.
AI.result: Stellar population is predominantly old and metal-rich: 75.6±9.5% of stellar mass formed >10 Gyr ago with median [M/H] ~ +0.35. Intermediate-age component at 2-3 Gyr contributes 20.8±8.7%, with minor populations at ~400 Myr (0.9±0.8%) and 20 Myr (3.6±1.4%). Systematic uncertainties from stellar models, binning, photometric range, binaries, and filter choice were assessed.
AI.conclusion: Results indicate early dominant formation, significant 2-3 Gyr episode, and minor recent star formation activity, consistent with spectroscopic measurements and properties of the inner nuclear star cluster and nuclear stellar disc.

title: Probing power spectrum enhancement at small scales with SKA
comment: 18 pages, 8 figures. Accepted for publication in ApJ
summary: The reionization process is driven by ionizing photons from dwarf galaxies in halos with virial temperature $T_{\rm vir} \gtrsim 10^4$ K, while minihalos whose $T_{\rm vir}\lesssim 10^4$ K consume ionizing photons and have negative contributions to reionization. Since ionizing sources and minihalos have different clustering characteristics, not only the reionization history, but also the morphology of the ionization field, is sensitive to the small-scale power spectrum. If the power spectrum at small scales is enhanced compared with the standard six-parameter $Λ$CDM model, then both the sources and sinks of ionizing photons would be boosted and the net impact depends on the competition between them. Therefore, the 21 cm signal that can probe the morphology of the ionization field will be a useful tool for detecting the small-scale power spectrum. Using the power spectrum proposed by Cielo et al. (2025) (C25) as a demonstration, we investigate the influence of small-scale power spectrum enhancement on the ionization field and the 21 cm signal. We find that for the C25 model, even under the constraints of observed UV luminosity functions for high-$z$ galaxies and reionization history, the 21~cm power spectrum and the bubble size distribution could be still significantly different from the regular $Λ$CDM model. The upcoming SKA-low AA* telescope, and a further imaging telescope, have the potential to detect the small-scale power spectrum more deeply.

AI.tldr: Enhanced small-scale power spectrum affects cosmic reionization morphology by boosting both ionizing sources (dwarf galaxies) and sinks (minihalos), with 21 cm signals potentially detecting these deviations from standard ΛCDM.
AI.motivation: The morphology of the ionization field during cosmic reionization is sensitive to the small-scale power spectrum, which affects both sources (dwarf galaxies) and sinks (minihalos) of ionizing photons differently. Understanding these effects is crucial for interpreting 21 cm signals and constraining cosmology beyond standard ΛCDM.
AI.method: Using the Cielo et al. (2025) power spectrum model as a demonstration, the study investigates how small-scale power spectrum enhancement influences the ionization field and 21 cm signals. The analysis considers constraints from observed UV luminosity functions for high-redshift galaxies and reionization history.
AI.result: Even under constraints from observed UV luminosity functions and reionization history, the C25 model shows significantly different 21 cm power spectrum and bubble size distribution compared to regular ΛCDM. The upcoming SKA-low AA* telescope and future imaging telescopes have potential to detect these small-scale power spectrum signatures.
AI.conclusion: 21 cm signals provide a powerful tool for probing small-scale power spectrum deviations from standard ΛCDM, with upcoming radio telescopes like SKA-low offering detection capabilities for these cosmological signatures through ionization field morphology measurements.

title: Ruling out conventional photoionization models in the closest LINER M31 with CFHT/SITELLE observations
comment: 15 pages, 10 figures, accepted for publication in ApJ
summary: The ionization mechanisms of low-ionization nuclear emission-line regions (LINERs), which are common in the local Universe, have been debated for decades. Our nearest large neighbor, M31, is classified as a LINER based on its optical emission line properties within the central kpc. In this work, we present a detailed photoionization modeling of the circumnuclear ionized gas in M31, explicitly tailored to its well-constrained physical conditions, including the absence of ongoing star formation and a currently inactive active galactic nucleus (AGN). Using spatially resolved CFHT/SITELLE observations, we find that photoionization by hot, evolved low-mass stars distributed throughout the bulge can roughly reproduce the observed radial intensity profiles of Hα, H\b{eta}, and [NII]. However, these models fail to match the observed [OIII] emission, producing radial profiles and [O III]/H\b{eta} ratios that are significantly steeper than observed. This discrepancy indicates a deficit of high-energy ionizing photons in standard stellar photoionization models, even with extended ionizing sources. We explore whether this tension can be alleviated by invoking either a bulge-filling, low-density ionized medium surrounding a denser Hα-emitting disk, or enhanced AGN activity in the recent past. While both scenarios can partially increase the [O III] emission, neither provides a fully satisfactory explanation under physically plausible conditions. Together with our earlier results for M81, these findings underscore persistent challenges in explaining LINER-like emission solely through conventional photoionization mechanisms.

AI.tldr: Photoionization modeling of M31's circumnuclear gas shows hot evolved stars can explain Hα and [NII] but fail to reproduce [OIII] emission, revealing a high-energy photon deficit in standard stellar models.
AI.motivation: To resolve the long-standing debate about ionization mechanisms in LINERs by studying M31, a nearby LINER with well-constrained physical conditions (no ongoing star formation, currently inactive AGN).
AI.method: Detailed photoionization modeling tailored to M31's physical conditions using spatially resolved CFHT/SITELLE observations, testing hot evolved low-mass stars as ionizing sources.
AI.result: Stellar photoionization models reproduce Hα, Hβ, and [NII] radial profiles but fail to match [OIII] emission, producing steeper radial profiles and higher [OIII]/Hβ ratios than observed. Neither a bulge-filling low-density medium nor enhanced past AGN activity fully resolves the discrepancy.
AI.conclusion: Standard stellar photoionization mechanisms cannot fully explain LINER-like emission in M31, revealing persistent challenges in understanding LINER ionization that align with similar findings in M81.

title: A New Window into the Baryon Cycle at Cosmic Noon with Line Intensity Mapping: Forecasts for auto- and cross-correlations in [CII]-158$μ$m, HI 21 cm, CO$_{J+1\rightarrow J}$, and H$α$ galaxies
comment: 43 pages, 7 figures, 4 tables. Submitted to the Journal of Cosmology and Astroparticle Physics
summary:
Across the peak of cosmic star formation at $z\sim1-2$, inflow, processing, and feedback drive rapid changes in the spatial distribution and chemical composition of baryons in galaxies and surrounding reservoirs; this baryon cycle can be tomographically mapped by line intensity mapping (LIM) of atomic hydrogen, ionized carbon, and carbon monoxide.
  We present a simulation-based forecasting framework for detecting auto- and cross-power spectra between spectroscopic surveys of four such tracers at $z\sim0.5-1.7$ mapping the same deep field - TIM, EoRSpec/FYST, MeerKAT, & Euclid. We forward-model 3-D distributions for these tracers from magnetohydrodynamic simulations, directly capturing the two-halo, one-halo, and shot statistics without relying on analytical decompositions. We further detail a signal-to-noise formalism, tailored to LIM surveys with highly anisotropic geometries and Fourier-space coverage.
  We demonstrate that galaxy cross-correlations will be the dominant discovery channel for current-generation surveys. These instruments will detect the auto-spectra for CO and HI 21 cm and the CO $\times$ 21 cm cross-spectrum at modest S/N $\sim 1-10$, while placing upper limits on the [CII]-158$μ$m signals. [CII], CO, and HI LIM will be $\sim3-30\times$ ($0.5-1.5$ dex) more sensitive to cross-correlation with the Euclid survey, however, than their respective auto-correlations, constraining all three models of line emission at high significance (S/N $\sim 10-40$) within this decade.
  Finally, we formulate a staged instrumental trajectory with planned or reasonable improvements, including the as-proposed SKA-Mid. We forecast advancing the per-$k$-mode sensitivities of each auto-, galaxy-line, and line-line spectrum by several orders of magnitude, enabling new percent- and sub-percent level constraints on cosmology and the redshift evolution of star formation and the baryon cycle.

AI.tldr: Forecasting framework for detecting auto- and cross-power spectra of multiple baryonic tracers (HI, [CII], CO) via line intensity mapping at z~0.5-1.7, showing cross-correlations with galaxy surveys will be dominant discovery channel for current instruments.
AI.motivation: To understand the baryon cycle during peak cosmic star formation (z~1-2) through tomographic mapping of multiple tracers (atomic hydrogen, ionized carbon, carbon monoxide) using line intensity mapping, as these tracers reveal different phases of baryonic processes including inflow, processing, and feedback.
AI.method: Simulation-based forecasting framework using magnetohydrodynamic simulations to forward-model 3D distributions of tracers (HI 21cm, [CII]-158μm, CO) without analytical decompositions. Signal-to-noise formalism tailored to LIM surveys with anisotropic geometries and Fourier-space coverage. Analysis of auto- and cross-power spectra for four spectroscopic surveys (TIM, EoRSpec/FYST, MeerKAT, Euclid).
AI.result: Current-generation surveys will detect CO and HI 21cm auto-spectra and CO×21cm cross-spectrum at S/N~1-10, with upper limits on [CII] signals. Cross-correlations with Euclid survey will be 3-30× more sensitive than auto-correlations, constraining all three line emission models at high significance (S/N~10-40) within this decade. Future improvements (including SKA-Mid) could advance per-k-mode sensitivities by orders of magnitude.
AI.conclusion: Galaxy cross-correlations are the dominant discovery channel for current LIM surveys, enabling high-significance constraints on baryon cycle evolution. Future instrumental improvements promise percent-level constraints on cosmology and redshift evolution of star formation and baryonic processes.

title: Weak lensing higher-order statistics to disentangle modified gravity and massive neutrinos
comment: 34 pages, 6 figures, 4 tables. To be submitted to JCAP
summary: Going beyond second order in weak lensing (WL) statistics is known to break degeneracies among cosmological parameters. We take a step further here, investigating whether higher-order statistics (HOS) in weak lensing can disentangle among General Relativity (GR) and modified gravity (MG), also taking into account the presence of massive neutrinos. To this end, we rely on mock convergence maps obtained from GR and $f(R)$ gravity N - body simulations, and we look for MG signatures in a wide set of higher-order WL probes. We rely on different metrics to quantify the discriminatory power of each probe, also varying the measurement setup. We find out that WL HOS can indeed disentangle MG and GR also in the presence of massive neutrinos.

AI.tldr: Higher-order weak lensing statistics can distinguish between General Relativity and modified gravity even with massive neutrinos present.
AI.motivation: To investigate whether higher-order statistics in weak lensing can disentangle General Relativity from modified gravity theories, particularly in the presence of massive neutrinos, which adds complexity to cosmological parameter degeneracies.
AI.method: Used mock convergence maps from GR and f(R) gravity N-body simulations, analyzed a wide set of higher-order weak lensing probes, employed different metrics to quantify discriminatory power, and varied measurement setups.
AI.result: Higher-order weak lensing statistics can indeed disentangle modified gravity from General Relativity even when massive neutrinos are present, demonstrating their discriminatory power across different measurement configurations.
AI.conclusion: Higher-order weak lensing statistics provide a robust tool for distinguishing between General Relativity and modified gravity theories, maintaining effectiveness even in cosmologies with massive neutrinos.

title: Filling the Gap in Cluster Evolution: JWST's Glimpse into a Young, Star-Forming Cluster at Cosmic Noon
comment: 25 pages; 13 figures, 1 Table; Submitted to ApJ. Comments are welcome!
summary: We present a detailed study of HUDFJ0332.4-2746.6 (HUDF46), a $z \approx 1.84$ overdensity in the Hubble Ultra Deep Field, previously identified with HST as a proto-cluster. JWST/NIRISS spectroscopy expands its confirmed membership from 18 to 37 galaxies, while deep HST/ACS, JWST/NIRCam, and JWST/MIRI imaging provide a comprehensive multiwavelength view from the rest-frame UV to the mid-infrared. This dataset probes the population across three dex in stellar mass ($M_\bigstar \approx 10^{7.5\text{--}10.5}\,M_\odot$), delivering the first direct view of a young cluster down to such low-$M_\bigstar$ at $z\gtrsim1$. Assuming virialization, we derive a velocity dispersion of $σ\approx 670\pm 91\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ and a halo mass of $M_{200} \approx (1.2\pm0.2) \times 10^{14}\,M_\odot$, in agreement with X-ray constraints from deep {\it Chandra} data. Despite residing in a massive halo likely in the hot-halo regime, the population is overwhelmingly star-forming, with no established red sequence and no extended X-ray emission from a hot intracluster medium. HUDF46 members have stellar and structural properties nearly indistinguishable from coeval field galaxies, and the structure hosts only one AGN candidate, found in its brightest galaxy, which lies at the cluster center. Overall, HUDF46 appears to be in a transitional phase prior to the onset of environmental quenching, making its galaxy population a key benchmark for tracing the processes that will later build a passive population and shape the assembly of massive clusters at later cosmic times.

AI.tldr: JWST study of z≈1.84 proto-cluster HUDF46 reveals 37 confirmed members with stellar masses spanning 10^7.5-10.5 M⊙, showing predominantly star-forming galaxies with no established red sequence despite massive halo mass of ~1.2×10^14 M⊙.
AI.motivation: To characterize the galaxy population in a young proto-cluster at z≈1.84 using comprehensive multiwavelength data from HST, JWST/NIRCam, JWST/MIRI, and JWST/NIRISS spectroscopy, probing down to low stellar masses to understand early cluster formation processes.
AI.method: Combined JWST/NIRISS spectroscopy to expand confirmed membership from 18 to 37 galaxies, with deep HST/ACS, JWST/NIRCam, and JWST/MIRI imaging providing rest-frame UV to mid-infrared coverage. Derived velocity dispersion and halo mass assuming virialization, compared with X-ray constraints from Chandra data.
AI.result: Velocity dispersion σ≈670±91 km/s, halo mass M200≈(1.2±0.2)×10^14 M⊙ consistent with X-ray constraints. Population overwhelmingly star-forming with no red sequence, minimal AGN activity (only one candidate), and galaxy properties indistinguishable from coeval field galaxies despite massive halo.
AI.conclusion: HUDF46 is in a transitional phase before environmental quenching onset, providing a key benchmark for tracing processes that will later build passive populations and shape massive cluster assembly at later cosmic times.

title: Discovery of a nearby radio relic in the low-mass, merging cluster Abell 4067
comment: 8 pages, 3 figures, 2 tables. Submitted to MNRAS Letters
summary: Shock waves generated during cluster mergers offer a powerful probe of how large-scale structure grows and evolves in the Universe. As part of the MeerKAT-South Pole Telescope (SPT) survey, we report the discovery of a single arc-like radio relic in the galaxy cluster Abell 4067 ($z=0.099$), one of the lowest-mass clusters known to host such a structure. MeerKAT UHF-band (0.58--1.09 GHz) observations reveal a relic with a largest linear size of $\sim 1.48 \pm 0.02$ Mpc, located at a projected distance of 0.95 Mpc from the cluster centre. XMM-Newton X-ray data show that the relic's position and orientation relative to the intracluster medium (ICM) elongation are consistent with a merger-driven shock-wave scenario. The relic has an estimated radio power of $3.10 \pm 0.03 \times 10^{24}$ W Hz$^{-1}$ at 150 MHz. When placed in the $P_{150\,\mathrm{MHz}}$--$M_{500}$ scaling relation, the Abell 4067 relic appears less luminous compared to relics in more massive clusters, suggesting an association with weak merger shocks. This finding supports the idea that relics in low-mass clusters may form through less energetic merger events, leading to weak merger shocks. This is further supported by the absence of a detectable central radio halo in Abell 4067, reinforcing the idea that luminous radio halos are not a universal outcome of cluster mergers and highlighting the role of cluster mass, merger energetics, and evolutionary stage in shaping diffuse radio emission in the intracluster medium.

AI.tldr: Discovery of a radio relic in low-mass cluster Abell 4067 reveals weak merger shocks and supports the idea that relic formation depends on cluster mass and merger energetics.
AI.motivation: To understand how large-scale structure grows and evolves in the Universe by studying shock waves generated during cluster mergers, particularly in low-mass clusters which are less commonly observed to host radio relics.
AI.method: Combined MeerKAT UHF-band (0.58-1.09 GHz) radio observations with XMM-Newton X-ray data to study Abell 4067, a low-mass cluster at z=0.099. Analyzed relic properties including size, location, orientation, and radio power, and compared to the P150MHz-M500 scaling relation.
AI.result: Discovered a 1.48 ± 0.02 Mpc radio relic in Abell 4067, one of the lowest-mass clusters known to host such a structure. The relic has radio power of 3.10 ± 0.03 × 10²⁴ W Hz⁻¹ at 150 MHz and appears less luminous in the scaling relation compared to relics in more massive clusters. No central radio halo was detected.
AI.conclusion: The findings support that relics in low-mass clusters form through less energetic merger events producing weak shocks. The absence of a radio halo reinforces that luminous radio halos are not universal outcomes of cluster mergers, highlighting the importance of cluster mass, merger energetics, and evolutionary stage in shaping diffuse radio emission.

title: Forecasting the cross correlation of Terahertz Intensity Mapper [CII] line intensity maps with Euclid galaxies
summary: We forecast that the Terahertz Intensity Mapper (TIM) cross-correlated with Euclid's Fornax deep field (EDF-F), TIM$\times$EDF-F, will detect the [CII]-galaxy cross-power spectrum at a median redshift of 1.1 with $\gtrsim 7 σ$ confidence. The Poisson component of the cross-power spectrum at $0.1 \leq k \leq 10$ hMpc$^{-1}$ (i.e. cross-shot noise) will be detected at $\gtrsim 3 σ$ in 4 bins spanning $0.5 < z< 1.7$. This measurement will constrain the mean [CII] specific intensity over half of cosmic history and assess the degree to which Euclid-selected galaxies account for the [CII] intensity observed by TIM. We find that TIM can detect the cross-power spectrum across a wide range of [CII] intensity models.

AI.tldr: TIM×EDF-F cross-correlation will detect [CII]-galaxy cross-power spectrum at z~1.1 with >7σ confidence, constraining mean [CII] specific intensity across cosmic history.
AI.motivation: To constrain the mean [CII] specific intensity over half of cosmic history and assess how Euclid-selected galaxies account for the [CII] intensity observed by TIM, enabling better understanding of cosmic star formation and galaxy evolution.
AI.method: Cross-correlation analysis between Terahertz Intensity Mapper (TIM) and Euclid's Fornax deep field (EDF-F) to measure the [CII]-galaxy cross-power spectrum, including Poisson component (cross-shot noise) across multiple redshift bins.
AI.result: TIM×EDF-F will detect the [CII]-galaxy cross-power spectrum at median redshift 1.1 with >7σ confidence, and the cross-shot noise component at >3σ in 4 redshift bins spanning 0.5<z<1.7, robust across various [CII] intensity models.
AI.conclusion: The cross-correlation measurement will provide strong constraints on cosmic [CII] emission and its connection to galaxy populations, enabling detailed studies of star formation history and galaxy evolution across cosmic time.

title: Single Parameter Model for Galaxy Rotation Curves
comment: 28 pages, 6 figures. Published in Galaxies Journal Feb 2026
summary: One key piece of evidence for dark matter is the rotation-curve problem: the disagreement between measured galactic rotation curves and their luminous mass. A novel solution to this problem is presented here, in a model that predicts observed Doppler-shifted spectra based only on the luminous matter estimates and one free model parameter. This model is applied to fit the rotation curves of the SPARC sample of 175 galaxies, yielding mass-to-light ratios, goodness of fit measurements, and the free parameter. The model's average reduced chi square compares favorably with the dark matter model for the same data, and more galaxies are successfully fit by this model. The model provides a useful formulation linking luminous matter to the observed rotation curves, with the dark matter contribution to galaxies encoded in two transformation terms of the luminous mass. It also offers a lower-parameter characterization of the rotation curve problem, and a power law relationship between the model's free parameter and galactic photometric quantities is observed, potentially removing the need for the free parameter.

AI.tldr: A novel model explains galactic rotation curves using only luminous matter and one free parameter, fitting SPARC data better than dark matter models and potentially eliminating need for free parameter.
AI.motivation: To address the rotation-curve problem (discrepancy between measured galactic rotation curves and luminous mass predictions) without invoking dark matter, offering an alternative explanation based solely on luminous matter.
AI.method: Developed a model predicting observed Doppler-shifted spectra using only luminous matter estimates and one free parameter. Applied to fit rotation curves of 175 galaxies from the SPARC sample, extracting mass-to-light ratios, goodness of fit measurements, and the free parameter.
AI.result: The model's average reduced chi square compares favorably with dark matter models for the same data, and more galaxies are successfully fit by this model. A power law relationship between the model's free parameter and galactic photometric quantities is observed, potentially removing the need for the free parameter.
AI.conclusion: The model provides a useful formulation linking luminous matter to observed rotation curves, with dark matter contribution encoded in two transformation terms of luminous mass. Offers a lower-parameter characterization of the rotation curve problem and potentially eliminates need for free parameter through discovered relationships.

title: First spectroscopic identification of the main sequence in Westerlund 1
comment: 20 pages, 10 figures, 4 tables. Accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics
summary: Being the most massive known young stellar cluster in the Milky Way, Westerlund 1 (Wd1) constitutes an ideal benchmark for understanding the evolution of massive stars. However, the cluster age remains highly controversial (~4-10 Myr), hindering the use of Wd1 as a reference for massive star evolution. One of the main issues is high foreground extinction, which has so far prevented the detection of the main sequence. Using infrared spectroscopy we seek to detect the cluster's main sequence for the first time, to characterise the Hertzsprung-Russell diagram, and to use the cluster's turn-off to obtain a robust age estimate. We obtained multi-epoch, near-infrared VLT/KMOS spectroscopic observations of Wd1 to map its population of massive stars. The spectra of ~110 members were analysed with CMFGEN models to derive stellar parameters, populate the cluster Hertzsprung-Russell diagram, and compare it with isochrones from evolutionary models. Our observations returned 47 new spectroscopically identified cluster members, with spectral types O9-B1 III-V. The cluster turn-off indicates an age of 5.5+/-1.0 Myr at a distance of 4.23+0.23-0.21 kpc, displaying a moderate degree of coevality. We demonstrate that our estimate of the age of Wd1 is robust against reasonable changes in the distance and extinction law, and the adopted rotational velocity and metallicity of the stellar isochrones. We further find that ~65% of the OB stars with multi-epoch coverage exhibit radial-velocity variability. Infrared observations of the unevolved stellar population support a single episode of star formation with an age of ~5.5 Myr, reinforcing its potential as a benchmark for massive star evolution and providing a reference sample for future binary population studies.

AI.tldr: Infrared spectroscopy of Westerlund 1 reveals its main sequence for the first time, yielding a robust age estimate of 5.5±1.0 Myr and establishing it as a benchmark for massive star evolution.
AI.motivation: Westerlund 1 is the most massive known young stellar cluster in the Milky Way, making it an ideal benchmark for understanding massive star evolution. However, its age remains highly controversial (4-10 Myr), primarily due to high foreground extinction preventing detection of the main sequence, which hinders its use as a reference for massive star evolution studies.
AI.method: Used multi-epoch, near-infrared VLT/KMOS spectroscopic observations to map the population of massive stars in Wd1. Analyzed spectra of ~110 members with CMFGEN models to derive stellar parameters, populate the cluster Hertzsprung-Russell diagram, and compare with evolutionary model isochrones. The approach specifically targeted detection of the cluster's main sequence for the first time.
AI.result: Identified 47 new spectroscopically confirmed cluster members with spectral types O9-B1 III-V. Determined cluster turn-off age of 5.5±1.0 Myr at a distance of 4.23+0.23-0.21 kpc, showing moderate coevality. The age estimate is robust against reasonable variations in distance, extinction law, rotational velocity, and metallicity. Found that ~65% of OB stars with multi-epoch coverage exhibit radial-velocity variability.
AI.conclusion: Infrared observations of the unevolved stellar population support a single episode of star formation at ~5.5 Myr, establishing Westerlund 1 as a robust benchmark for massive star evolution and providing a reference sample for future binary population studies.

title: Direct VLBI Detection of Interstellar Turbulence Imprint on a Quasar: TXS 2005+403
summary: We report the first unambiguous detection of refractive substructure in an active galactic nucleus (AGN) using ground-based Very Long Baseline Interferometry (VLBI). Our analysis of TXS 2005+403 - observed at 1--5 GHz along a line of sight through the Cygnus region - reveals clear signatures of turbulence-induced substructure on long baselines that cannot be explained by the smooth scatter-broadened profile from diffractive effects alone. This signal persists across multiple observations spanning 2010-2019, demonstrating stable scattering properties along the line of sight. The combination of high flux density, compact intrinsic structure, and strong scattering establishes TXS 2005+403 as an exceptional laboratory for probing Galactic turbulence. This detection demonstrates that AGNs can serve as cosmic lighthouses illuminating interstellar plasma across the sky, complementing pulsar scintillation studies and informing scattering mitigation for millimeter-wavelength imaging of Sagittarius A*.

AI.tldr: First detection of refractive substructure in an AGN using ground-based VLBI, revealing turbulence-induced scattering in the Cygnus region that persists over 9 years.
AI.motivation: To detect and characterize refractive substructure in AGNs caused by interstellar plasma turbulence, complementing pulsar scintillation studies and informing scattering mitigation for millimeter-wavelength imaging of objects like Sagittarius A*.
AI.method: Analysis of TXS 2005+403 using ground-based Very Long Baseline Interferometry (VLBI) at 1-5 GHz frequencies, observing along a line of sight through the Cygnus region, with data spanning 2010-2019.
AI.result: Clear detection of refractive substructure on long baselines that cannot be explained by smooth scatter-broadened profiles alone, demonstrating stable scattering properties over 9 years and establishing TXS 2005+403 as an exceptional laboratory for studying Galactic turbulence.
AI.conclusion: AGNs can serve as cosmic lighthouses for probing interstellar plasma turbulence across the sky, providing complementary data to pulsar scintillation studies and valuable insights for scattering mitigation in high-frequency astronomical imaging.
